python-model.python: Python owns execution; model work uses its configured device and executor.
python-model.swift: The Mac authors, submits and inspects Python results; no native implementation of this managed operation is claimed.
python-model.notes: CUDA is the comparison reference. This inventory records no configuration-specific cross-backend qualification. Try supported Python execution with that limitation stated; exact device admission remains owner-specific.

python-cpu.python: Python CPU owner; no GPU is required for this operation.
python-cpu.swift: Use the shared Python path from the Mac and inspect its records; a native twin is not required for authoring equivalence.
python-cpu.notes: CPU execution on a Mac is not MPS or MLX qualification. Numerical correctness and input roles still need owner tests.

diagnostic-model.python: Python model diagnostic on the selected device; local and Slurm routing use existing owners.
diagnostic-model.swift: Mac science execution/custody controls drive Python and read the exported report; native numerical diagnostic parity is not yet supplied.
diagnostic-model.notes: Stability measures direction sensitivity; a battery measures its declared capability/generation checks. Neither is universal behavioral validation.

reader.python: Python reader fitting/scoring, with model activation capture on its selected device.
reader.swift: Native fitting/scoring separates final-test rows from sign/layer selection and preserves evidence roles across clients.
reader.notes: Cross-client role fixtures and synthetic fitting tests establish the split contract; they do not qualify model-level numerical agreement.

training.python: Python LoRA training on the selected engine device; adapter-family admission is explicit.
training.swift: Native MLX LoRA training exists; use the training recipe matrix to compare objectives, scaling and data treatment.
training.notes: New native training stamps the direct adapter multiplier. Objectives, schedules, evidence admission and adapter formats remain distinct; no trained-weight equivalence is claimed.

jlens.python: Python owns acquisition/import, model reference qualification and runtime readout; metadata-only steps do not establish device coverage.
jlens.swift: The app acquires, inspects and presents Python lens evidence. PyTorch/HF-native atoms are not assumed valid for MLX activations.
jlens.notes: The catalog entry groups multiple actions: qualify model-dependent paths separately from CPU metadata/import. Matching dimensions alone does not justify representation transfer.

sae-import.python: Python owns Gemma Scope analysis and feature import; distinguish reading/importing tensors from model execution.
sae-import.swift: Mac UI drives Python operations and inspects imported evidence; no native Gemma Scope numerical implementation is asserted.
sae-import.notes: Successful import alone does not qualify SAE feature behavior on MPS or validate transferring a feature into MLX activations.

jspace.python: Python J-space analysis: intervention-dependent downstream residual readout using a qualified lens.
jspace.swift: The Mac authors the request and displays Python reports; no native MLX J-space numerical implementation is supplied.
jspace.notes: J-space is distinct from OptVec training. The current batch owner accepts OptVec artifact metadata for layer/dose; this is an admission limitation, not a definition of the method.

campaign.python: CPU materialization/coordination; training cells execute as separate Python GPU jobs.
campaign.swift: Mac authoring and campaign controls drive Python; the initial CPU plan is not the training run.
campaign.notes: Do not infer MPS campaign scheduling support from a training kernel. Cell execution and local/Slurm orchestration need separate qualification.

stability.python: Python model diagnostic on the selected device; local and Slurm routing use existing owners.
stability.swift: Native ExtractStability captures pinned inputs and reports row/order sensitivity through steerlab-cli experiment extract-stability. The existing Mac science job sheet continues to drive Python.
stability.notes: Shared seeds and numerical fixture results establish implementation parity; actual model/backend comparisons remain unqualified.

probe-library.python: Shared read-only probe artifact inspection; no model or GPU is loaded.
probe-library.swift: The Probes section and native CLI use the same portable owner via the local client runtime.
probe-library.notes: Legacy bytes and unknown provenance remain unchanged. Library inspection is not model execution or cross-backend qualification.

steering.title: Chat with a model and steer it with a vector
steering.notes: Additive injection and ablation share mechanics and scope descriptors on both engines. CPU/MPS hooks have a scoped comparison; native cross-backend qualification remains pending.

extraction.title: Build a concept vector from example texts
extraction.notes: Both engines implement the extraction recipes. Three recipes have a scoped CPU/MPS capture comparison, not a full qualification. Vectors do not transfer between engines.

measured-generation.title: Run a study's measured generation
measured-generation.notes: Both engines record the effective per-record seed policy. The same surface intent does not establish identical numerical output.

multi-agent.title: Run a scenario in which several agents take turns
multi-agent.notes: Both engines derive seeds per turn with common streams across conditions. Live full-transcript qualification remains pending.

sweep.title: Search layers and strengths with a sweep
sweep.notes: Both engines run sweeps through their stage owners. Inspect artifacts and effective configuration; the engines are not numerically interchangeable.

probeMeasurements.label: Probe measurements
probeMeasurements.notes: Probe readings recorded while a study generates. The engine built into the app refuses a study that declares them before it loads a model.

interventionPolicies.label: Agents with intervention policies
interventionPolicies.notes: A policy changes steering while the agent generates. The engine built into the app refuses an agent that carries one.

saeLatentArms.label: SAE latent arms
saeLatentArms.notes: Arms that steer with a sparse-autoencoder feature. The engine built into the app refuses a study that declares them, rather than run its other arms alone.

jlensReadout.label: J-lens readout
jlensReadout.notes: What a run reads out of the residual stream while it generates. The engine built into the app refuses a study that declares one before it loads a model.
